newsitem.title: PERU: Peru Prime Minister denies cabinet resignations.
newsitem.headline: Peru Prime Minister denies cabinet resignations.

text.p: Prime Minister Alberto Pandolfi Tuesday denied media reports that a group of ministers had resigned from Peru's cabinet.

"There are no resignations," Pandolfi told journalists after weekend newspapers reported that up to six ministers had resigned during an extraordinary cabinet meeting with President Alberto Fujimori last Friday.
"The cabinet continues to work well. The results of the ministers, guided by the president, are evident in the country's macroeconomic figures," Pandolfi said.

The prime minister cited latest government figures showing year-on-year economic growth of 7.3 percent in the first four months of 1997, compared to a 1.8 percent rise in the same period in 1996, as a clear sign Peru was on course for sustained development.

Fujimori's cabinet of ministers currently has one vacant post following Fisheries Minister Carlos Boggiano's resignation last month due to health reasons. Boggiano's replacement would probably be announced later this week, Pandolfi said.
